what: The Certificate Maker creates printable certificates for schools, clubs, courses, events and workplaces. Pick a type, such as achievement, participation, appreciation, completion or excellence, and the title and wording fill in for you. Every line can be changed.

Choose from five designs (Classic, Elegant, Modern, Bold and Minimal), a colour, a name style and A4 or US Letter in landscape or portrait. Add your logo, a seal and up to two signatures, typed in a script font or added as a picture.

Paste a list of names, one per line, and download a single PDF with one certificate per person. Use the arrows above the preview to check each name, and save any one certificate as a PNG to share online.
uses: Award certificates to a whole class in one go, such as for reading or attendance.
Give completion certificates to every participant.
Make participation and winner certificates for all entrants.
Thank staff and volunteers with certificates of appreciation.
Celebrate players of the season and team achievements.
tutorial: Tap Achievement, Participation, Appreciation, Completion, Excellence or Custom. The title, line above the name and description fill in.
Change the title, the line above the name and the description. Type {name} in the description to include the person's name.
Paste or type the names, one per line. Blank lines are skipped.
Type your organisation and the date, and add a logo if you have one.
Type the signer's name and role. Add a picture of the signature, or leave it and the name is written in script.
Choose a design, colour, name style, paper size and orientation, and turn the seal on or off.
Use the arrows to see each name, then press Download PDF for all of them or "This one as PNG".
features: Up to 500 names, one page each, in a single PDF.
Classic, Elegant, Modern, Bold and Minimal.
Achievement, participation, appreciation, completion and excellence.
Typed in script or uploaded, with the white background removed.
An award seal in your colour and your own logo.
Names, logos and signatures never leave your device.

example.title: Worked example: certificates for a coding club
example.text: A teacher picks Participation, pastes 28 student names, types "Riverside Coding Club" and the date, and adds the head teacher's signature photo and her own typed name. She chooses the Modern design in blue on A4 landscape, checks a few names with the arrows and presses Download PDF. certificates-28.pdf has 28 pages, one per student, ready to print.

tips: Check the spelling of every name with the arrows before printing.
Print on thick paper or card (160 gsm or more) for a quality feel.
Use the Serif or Modern sans name style for names with letters outside the Latin alphabet.
Keep the description to one or two lines so the certificate stays clean.
Print at 100% or "Actual size" so the borders are not cut off.
problems: Long names are shrunk to fit the line. Use a shorter form, such as a first name and family name only.
My signature has a grey box around it
Use a photo with plain white paper and good light, or a PNG with a transparent background.
Some letters show as "?" in the PDF
The script fonts cover Latin letters only. Choose the Serif or Modern sans name style.
Hundreds of names can take a few seconds. Keep the page open until the download starts.
